title: C626 — Right exterior mirror connector
introduction:
There is more going on here than glass on a stalk. The right exterior mirror reference includes movement, heating, lighting, position sensing, folding and a blindspot warning indicator. I use those function names to understand what a row concerns before looking at its circuit and cavity identifiers. An entry in this reference does not prove that every listed feature is fitted to a particular car.

Read the identification table first, then use the connector face and harness table to orient yourself within the reference. Match a drawn cavity label to its assignment rows and read each row across. Several cavity labels have multiple entries; keep those entries separate rather than imagining extra physical sockets or assuming the circuits are joined. Preserve the IF PLUS conditions and the printed positive and negative signs.

The pigtail table provides a separate parts reference. This page does not establish physical viewing direction, access, test conditions, wire selection, kit interchangeability or installation methods. Gauge conventions and Size and Used codes remain in their printed notation. Where repeated rows lack applicability information, this guide leaves that choice unresolved. The metadata Pin Count differs from the cavity count shown by the drawing and both pigtail records; the source does not reconcile that difference.

edits.why: The drawing has a rounded rectangular face with parallel columns of cavity labels, a large loop-shaped projection on the page's left and smaller projections around the housing. I use those asymmetrical features as landmarks within this drawing so that I do not casually reverse its arrangement. Their mechanical functions are unlabeled, so they are not instructions for releasing the connector. The adjacent identification table associates the illustrated face with its harness and housing reference; it does not establish the physical viewing side.

Use Cavity to find the drawn position, Circuit Number to identify the circuit and Function to understand the row's role. Keep its color, gauge, qualifier, usage entry and terminal reference together. The named functions distinguish mirror movement from position sensing, heating, lamps, folding and warning indication; those roles should not be collapsed into a generic mirror-power connection. Likewise, retain the distinction between the ground entry and the separately named return entries. The protection entry describes a fuse-or-circuit-breaker supply. Repeated cavity entries include different circuits, colors or functions, and blank qualifiers do not tell us which applies to a particular car. The puddle-lamp entry's left-side wording is retained pending review rather than silently changed to match the article title.

I read Number, Service Part and Engineering Shell as separate identifiers: the kit listing, its service-part reference and its housing reference. Gauge, Material, Cavities and Image describe the listed assembly in the table's own terms. The image filenames identify referenced illustrations; they do not supply a visible comparison of the kits here. A shared engineering-shell entry alone does not settle interchangeability. Use this table to carry the listed identifiers into a parts-applicability check, not to choose between the kits or begin a splice repair.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata Pin Count differs from the distinct cavity positions in the drawing and the pigtail table's cavity total. Repeated assignment rows may account for the metadata total, but its meaning is undefined; do not equate it with physical housing capacity.

The right exterior mirror article contains a puddle-lamp function explicitly labeled LEFT. The supplied evidence does not resolve whether the function wording or its association with this connector is incorrect.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 48 primary units, three complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. Count, repeated assignments and left-puddle-lamp label ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
